title: Line-up templates | Kaderblick Docs

hero.heading: Line-up templates
hero.lead: Under Line-ups, you prepare reusable formations for a team in Kaderblick. A template contains positions, bench, assigned players and tactical notes. The specific match line-up is then created for the relevant match.

body:
Use the overview

  • Team: limits templates to one team. “All teams” also shows templates without a fixed team.
  • Active: usable templates; the tab number is their count.
  • Archive: stored templates that can be restored or permanently deleted.
  • Template card: shows pitch preview, name, formation, field and bench player counts and notes.
  • Pitch or Edit: opens the line-up editor.
  • Tactics board: opens the tactical display.
  • Three-dot menu: Edit, Duplicate, Archive and Delete. Duplicating asks for a copy name.

Create a template

  1. 1
    Open a new template
    Select New template in the top-right corner.
  2. 2
    Choose basic data
    Enter a clear name, choose the team and then a formation system.
  3. 3
    Distribute players
    Drag players from the squad to a field position or bench. Move them again to correct placement.
  4. 4
    Add notes
    Record tactical information that remains with the template.
  5. 5
    Save
    Check pitch and bench and select Save.

Available formations are 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 3-5-2, 5-3-2 and 4-1-4-1. No template starts without preset positions.

Work in the editor

  • Squad: players available for the selected team; up to 36 can appear.
  • Pitch: holds eleven starting positions. Move players with mouse or touch.
  • Bench: contains intended substitutes.
  • Auto-place: distributes suitable players to free positions. Review afterwards.
  • Snap points: help place players in intended zones.
  • Position colours and zones: distinguish defence, midfield and attack.

Plan tactics globally and for a match

The tactics board is a planning tool in its own right. You can prepare tactics permanently on a line-up template or plan them directly for the starting line-up and every later phase of a specific match.

Plan tactics on a line-up template

Under Line-ups, open the Tactics board on the required template card. Tactics saved there belong to the global template and remain available for future matches.

Plan tactics for a specific match

Open the match Match plan and select Tactics on the starting line-up or a later match phase. Anything saved there belongs only to that match phase.

Use the tactics board

  • Choose a full or half pitch.
  • Add your players, opponents and the ball, then move them on the pitch.
  • Draw passing routes, running routes and zones in one of six colours.
  • Arrange the plan in numbered steps. Undo and redo correct changes; delete removes the selected element.
  • Use presentation mode to show the tactical steps without editing tools.
  • Save the tactic before closing the screen.

Transfer tactics between a template and a match

Tactics from template copies only the tactics from a global line-up template into the selected match phase. The line-up and template remain unchanged; existing tactics in that match phase are replaced. Conversely, Save as template makes a match line-up globally reusable and lets you decide whether to copy its tactics.

Use line-ups in the match plan

Create a starting lineup for a match

  1. Open the match and its Starting lineup in the match plan.
  2. Select Choose formation or Edit. Use 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 3-5-2, 5-3-2, 4-1-4-1 or start without a preset.
  3. Load template copies an active lineup template into the match. Later match-plan changes do not alter the template.
  4. Assign the players for this match to the pitch and bench, then save.
  5. Share with players controls whether players may see the match plan.

Plan substitutions and changes

Under Match formations, select New formation, enter its minute and label, and choose the source formation. The new phase initially copies all players and positions from that source. Then adjust substitutions, positions and shape. This creates a chronological plan after the starting lineup.

How playing minutes are calculated

The starting lineup determines who is on the pitch from minute 0. Actual substitution events determine each subsequent playing interval. Kaderblick calculates completed minutes once the match is marked as finished, using half length and recorded added time. A planned later formation does not replace a recorded substitution.

If a player is missing

Check the team filter, then the player’s active team assignment. Its period must match team and season.
